adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:442 — Unsubscribing changes the logged-in user's notification settings through a predictable GET request without a token, allowing an attacker to change subscriptions without consent; use a CSRF-protected POST.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new GET route at 't/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe' (config/routes.rb:442) that maps to topics#unsubscribe. The controller action in app/controllers/topics_controller.rb modifies the user's TopicUser notification_level and calls tu.save! - this is a state-changing operation performed via GET request. The route is added to skip_before_filter :check_xhr (line 30), and while the controller requires authentication (ensure_logged_in is not skipped for unsubscribe), the action modifies user data through a simple GET request without CSRF protection. This is a legitimate security concern - an attacker could craft a link that, when clicked by a logged-in user, would change their notification settings for any topic.
